items.title: Rights panel steps in to address alleged contamination of well water near temple
points: The State Pollution Control Board (PCB) and the temple committee office-bearers assured the Commission that the issue of water contamination would be permanently resolved once the new waste treatment plant at the temple becomes operational.
The Commission directed the Sreemoolanagaram panchayat secretary to submit a report after testing a sample of well water from the temple’s neighbourhood once the treatment plant becomes operational.

The directive was issued on a petition filed by Sujikumar, a resident living around 300 metres from the temple entrance, alleging that the water in his well became polluted during the temple festival.
The Kochi Sub-Collector submitted a report to the Commission, informing that the Kochi Devaswom Board, PCB, and the Sreemoolanagaram panchayat had been instructed to take emergency measures.
The report stated that a wastewater storage tank with a capacity of 6 lakh litres had been constructed.
The PCB has directed the temple to use the treated water for agricultural purposes.
The 2026 festival will serve as a full-scale test to assess the plant’s efficiency.

items.title: Two SPOs go missing in J&K's Kishtwar; massive search operation launched
points: Two Special Police Officers (SPOs) went missing from the higher reaches of Dachhan in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district on Wednesday (November 12, 2026), prompting security forces to launch a massive joint search operation to trace them, officials said.

The missing personnel have been identified as Babi Chand (57) and Rashpal Kumar (45), both of whom were posted with the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the local police at their Kiyar village in Dachhan, the officials said.
They said the two SPOs were travelling from Kiyar camp to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah when they failed to reach their destination.
Following their disappearance, a massive search operation was launched jointly by the police and the Army's Rashtriya Rifles to locate the missing personnel.
According to the figures available, five people -- four terrorists and one Army soldier -- were killed in terror-related incidents in 2026.
In 2025, the toll stood at four, comprising three terrorists and one Army soldier.
In 2024, three security personnel and two civilians lost their lives.

items.title: Stand-Up India and Mudra Yojana extended by Union Cabinet for 5 more years
points: According to the government, the Credit Guarantee Fund for Stand-Up India will guarantee loans above ₹10 lakh and up to ₹1 crore for women and SC/ST entrepreneurs setting up greenfield enterprises.
The scheme targets an average of two loans per bank branch—one to a woman entrepreneur and one to an SC/ST entrepreneur.
The guarantee fee will be 0.50% annually, with no additional risk premium, while the guarantee cover will be increased to 85% across loan sizes.
Borrowers will also receive support through the loan process and business cycle.
Meanwhile, the PMMY Credit Guarantee Fund is expected to support Mudra loans worth ₹12.60 lakh crore.
It will cover PMMY loans of up to ₹20 lakh, overdrafts of up to ₹10,000 under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana and self-help group loans of ₹10-20 lakh, all without collateral.
The annual guarantee fee will be reduced from 1% to 0.75%, while the government plans to strengthen the claim process for lenders to improve credit flow to micro entrepreneurs.

items.title: Stock recommendations for 12 November from MarketSmith India
points: Stock market recap: Indian equities closed higher on Wednesday, with the Sensex gaining 772.75 points to 81,879.40 and the Nifty 50 rising 210.40 points to 25,255.05, as markets reopened after the Diwali-Balipratipada holiday.
Sustained foreign institutional buying was a key driver, with inflows totalling about ₹53,170 crore over six trading sessions in November.
Better-than-expected September-quarter earnings, with Nifty 50 companies posting nearly 24% profit growth, further lifted sentiment.
Among Nifty 50 constituents, M&M (+5.30%), IndiGo (+4.33%) and Trent (+3.32%) were the top gainers.
Adani Ports (-1.84%), ICICI Bank (-1.10%) and Tech Mahindra (-0.91%) led the losses, though overall market breadth remained positive.
The 21-day SMA has also crossed above the 50-day SMA, while the index trades about 5% above its 200-day SMA.

Foreign institutional buying and softer crude oil prices remain supportive, but higher-than-expected US inflation, Treasury yields near 5% and rising expectations of a Fed rate hike could temper risk appetite.

items.title: Rare IPO Bets on End of War and Economic Crisis in Myanmar
points: (Bloomberg) -- A Myanmar company is going public in the middle of a civil war and economic downturn, betting on an eventual recovery.
Concordia Pcl expects to raise about $200,000 in an initial public offering that will pave the way for Myanmar’s first main-board stock listing in more than three years.
That compares with about $1.2 million raised in the bourse’s first IPO in 2018.
The exchange began allowing foreigners to trade shares in 2020, shortly before the pandemic and military takeover disrupted Myanmar’s economy.
Local retail investors accounted for 99.86% of investors as of March, compared with just 0.14% for foreign retail investors, according to data compiled by the ASEAN Capital Markets Forum.
Average daily trading value was only about $11,000.
The benchmark Myanpix index has averaged in the 800-point range this year, compared with a 400-point range over the previous three years, according to YSX Chief Operating Officer Min Thu.

items.title: 1 Killed, Another Injured In Firing Over Land Dispute In UP: Cops
points: A 22-year-old man was killed and another injured after a group of people allegedly opened fire following a dispute in Bisana village under Chandpa police station area here on Wednesday evening, police said.
The incident took place around 8.30 pm when a dispute broke out between two groups of villagers.
One side allegedly opened fire, killing Manvendra (22) and injuring Sameer (22).
Sameer was referred to a higher medical facility after preliminary treatment, police said.

Superintendent of Police Chiranjiv Nath Sinha said preliminary investigation suggested that three to four people had visited the victim's house, where an argument broke out before one of them opened fire.
A land dispute is suspected to be the motive behind the incident, he said.
The SP said teams, including the Special Operations Group (SOG), have been formed to arrest the accused.

items.title: Oil Steadies After Slump as Iran War Talks Make Little Progress
points: Oil steadied as hostilities between Iran and the US remained muted with no indication of progress in peace talks.
West Texas Intermediate traded near $86 a barrel, after rising 0.6% on Wednesday, while Brent settled below $93.

Iran won’t remove “a single atom” of enriched nuclear material from the country, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaee said in an interview with Al Mayadeen, addressing one of the key US conditions for negotiations.
Brent is up more than 50% this year, but prices have reversed sharply in November on hopes the conflict will ease and as Persian Gulf energy shipments rise.
Saudi Arabia, the world’s largest crude exporter, told OPEC its production rose 26% in October to one of the highest monthly levels in years.

items.title: Index Provider MSCI Removes Strategy From Equity Benchmark
points: MSCI Inc. has dropped Strategy Inc. from its global equity benchmarks, potentially triggering billions of dollars in stock sales and adding fresh pressure to the financing model behind Michael Saylor’s vast Bitcoin holdings.

Strategy is among the firms that the major index provider is removing its MSCI USA Index after it adopted new eligibility rules, according to results of the November 2026 Index Review for the MSCI Equity Indexes released Wednesday.
Strategy has said it expects the firm’s class A common stock to be excluded from the MSCI Indexes as part of the review, according to the quarterly report in late October.
Shares of Strategy fell almost 2% in after-hours trading.
Bitcoin has dropped around 15% during the same period.
Pioneered by Saylor, Strategy’s co-founder and executive chairman, the firm has acquired over $60 billion in Bitcoin since the middle of 2020.
Last year, JPMorgan estimated that such an event could trigger as much as $2.8 billion of Strategy sales, and potentially another $8.8 billion if other indexes follow suit.

items.title: Thousands struggling without water after a major leak in a pipeline in Kolkata’s Tala area
points: Thousands of residents at Kolkata’s Tala area have been struggling without water for the last three days after a major water supply pipeline under the Tala bridge leaked.
According to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, over 5 million gallons of water have been gushed out after the 72-inch pipeline got damaged on Monday (November 9, 2026) morning.
Water supply to neighbourhoods of Central Avenue, Rajabazar, College Street, Bidhan Sarani, Park Circus, AJC Bose Road, parts of Ballygunge got disrupted, said the KMC officials.
KMC also started the repair work but said that it may take two to three days to restore the entire system.
The Tala reservoir can restore up to 44 million gallons of water and supply potable water to five booster pumping stations.

Taking immediate cognisance of the incident, General Manager, Eastern Railway, Gitika Pandey, held discussions at the highest level of State Government of West Bengal and initiated immediate action by constituting a dedicated team to tackle the situation.

items.title: "Farmers Always Top Priority": PM As Cabinet Clears Rabi Fertiliser Subsidy
points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday hailed the Union Cabinet's approval of Nutrient-Based Subsidy rates for the rabi 2026-27 season for phosphatic and potassic fertilisers, emphasising that farmers are always the government's top priority.
PM Modi stated that even in challenging global circumstances, the central government is leaving no stone unturned to improve farmers' lives.
"The nation's farmers have always been the top priority of the government," he said in a post on X.
In this direction, the Prime Minister said the Nutrient-Based Subsidy on fertilisers for the rabi 2026-27 season has been approved by the Union Cabinet.
This is approximately Rs 24,417.73 crore more than the budgetary requirement for the rabi 2025-26 season.
(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by NDTV staff and is published from a syndicated feed.)

items.title: Offering food, best dharma
points: Offering food to others is the best dharma, said R.
There is nothing to equal this, says Tiruvalluvar.
In his Tirumanthiram, Tirumoolar says we should offer a vilva leaf to Lord Siva, grass to a cow, and food to fellow human beings.
Tiruvalluvar says that even nectar, which confers immortality, must be shared with others.
Ilayankudi Maranar was one of the 63 Nayanmars praised by Sekkizhar in his Periya Puranam.
The Lord wanted to show the world how generous Ilayankudi Maranar could be even in poverty.
That night, Siva, in the guise of a Saivite devotee, arrived at Maranar’s doorstep.
When the couple was about to serve food, the sleeping guest woke and revealed Himself as Lord Siva.

items.title: Haryana Congress to launch campaign to protect people’s voting rights, says Sanjay Dutt
points: Haryana Congress will launch ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ campaign from November 12 to November 24 in the State, for what it terms an initiative to defend democracy, protect people’s voting rights and expose alleged electoral manipulation.

All India Congress Committee (AICC) in-charge of Haryana Sanjay Dutt and Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee president Rao Narender Singh will lead the two-week tour, participating in ‘Chaupals’ (community gatherings) across Haryana.
Mr. Dutt said the objective is to engage with people and mobilise public opinion in defence of democratic institutions and electoral integrity.
“The campaign assumes particular significance in Haryana, where the Congress party has raised serious questions about the integrity of the 2024 Assembly elections.
Congress maintains that the people’s mandate in favour of the party was subverted through a systematic conspiracy of electoral manipulation,” he said in a statement.

Through these ‘Chaupals’, the Congress will expose electoral irregularities, sensitise citizens about the dangers of manipulated electoral rolls and build a statewide movement to safeguard every citizen’s fundamental democratic right to vote.

items.title: US Treasury may allow purchase of sanctioned tankers on case basis
points: The US Treasury Department may allow companies to buy sanctioned shipping vessels and return them to legitimate shipping on a case-by-case basis, according to a government source and a person with knowledge of the matter.

“Treasury may consider proposals from legitimate shipping actors to purchase and restore shadow fleet vessels to the licit shipping industry on a case-by-case basis,” a US official told Platts, part of S&P Global Energy.
Another source with knowledge of the matter said Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control could be targeting 50-80 sanctioned tankers owned by non-sanctioned companies.
At the end of September, there were a total of 1,225 tankers sanctioned by the US, UK or EU, S&P Global Commodities at Sea(opens in a new tab) said in an Oct.
Of those, 560 were sanctioned by the US.
In 2026, 41 shadow-fleet crude tankers entered compliant trade through Oct.
20, with 68% remaining fully compliant so far, compared with just 17.5% of vessels that remained compliant in 2025.

items.title: Baltic Dry Index Up for 6th Day
points: The Baltic Exchange’s dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, rose by 3.4% to its highest since October 8 at 2,959 points, extending gains for the sixth consecutive session.
The capesize index, which typically transports 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, climbed by 5.5% to a peak since October 5 at 4,700 points.
Concurrently, the panamax index, which usually carries 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, rose by 1.4% to its highest since October 23 at 2,103 points.
Among smaller vessels, the supramax index edged up by 0.2% to 1,810 points, halting a 11-session losing run.

items.title: Woman found dead at locked flat in Baranagar; police suspect sexual assault
points: A 26-year-old woman was found dead at a flat in Kolkata’s Baranagar area on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) with the police suspecting she was sexually assaulted before the murder.
According to the police, the flat is owned by the victim’s sister and brother-in-law, who had been staying there for the last four years.
However, they had recently moved to Hooghly for their work.
“Two days ago, her brother-in-law handed over the key to a lady.
But the victim took the key from her on Tuesday and went to the flat at the fifth floor of the apartment,” said a police official from Baranagar Police Station.
Upon receiving the information, the police arrived at the apartment late on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) night and broke open the door to recover her body.
Reacting to the development, the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress alleged that the local BJP leaders are trying to downplay the gravity of the incident.

items.title: Hoax note on Air India Kolkata-Mumbai flight sparks hijack scare
points: The note was found by the cabin crew of flight AI 2772, an Airbus A320 (VT-TNH), at around 10.37am, when it was scheduled to depart.
It warned that the aircraft would be hijacked at 11.10am, officials said.

All 105 passengers and seven crew members were deboarded and security personnel thoroughly searched the aircraft to rule out any potential threat “as per established protocols,” the official quoted above said.
In its initial statement, Airports Authority of India (AAI), confirmed that a hijack note was found and that concerned agencies were carrying out checks.

An updated statement in the evening said, “Following the completion of all necessary checks as per established protocols, boarding for Air India flight AI 2772 (Kolkata–Mumbai) is complete at NSCBI Airport, Kolkata.
The expected time of departure (ETD) is 1700 hrs.” The aircraft eventually took off for Mumbai at 5.38pm, the airport authorities confirmed.

items.title: Madras High Court sets aside one-month simple imprisonment imposed on IAS officer Anshul Mishra in contempt proceedings
points: A Division Bench of the Madras High Court has set aside an order passed by a single judge who found Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Anshul Mishra guilty of contempt of court proceedings and directed him to undergo simple imprisonment for one month.
Nisha Banu (now a judge of Kerala High Court) and S.
Sounthar had on September 15, 2025 allowed a contempt appeal filed by the IAS officer and permitted him to withdraw ₹25,000 which he had deposited in the court while filing the appeal.
According to the siblings, 17 cents of their land abutting Nesapakkam Road in Chennai was acquired in 1983 for constructing Tamil Nadu Housing Board tenements.

Pursuant to a writ petition filed in 2003, followed by contempt proceedings, about 10.5 cents of the land was reconveyed to them but the rest of 6.5 cents was retained for the purpose of widening the Nesapakkam Road.

items.title: CII Partnership Summit: CM Naidu seeks WIPO’s support to boost innovation ecosystem in A.P.

Mr. Naidu proposed establishing a WIPO–Andhra Pradesh Academy to conduct joint training programmes on patents, trademarks, industrial designs, and technology protection tailored for students, researchers, startup founders, and Micro, Small and Medium…

Seeking international exposure for local heritage products, Mr. Naidu urged WIPO to help the State secure Geographical Indication (GI) tags for its traditional handloom and handicraft sectors while elevating quality standards and global branding for…

Highlighting key initiatives, including the Ratan Tata Innovation Hub and the grassroots ‘Swayam’ brand aimed at fostering 10 lakh women entrepreneurs, Mr. Naidu invited WIPO to partner in expanding women-led business enterprises.

items.title: CII Partnership Summit: Andhra CM Naidu makes investment pitch before UAE, Japanese delegations
points: Chandrababu Naidu during a meeting with Japanese Ambassador Keiichi Ono in Visakhapatnam on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGMENT Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N.
Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday met UAE Minister of Economy and Tourism Abdullah bin Touq Al Marri, who is in Visakhapatnam to participate in the CII Partnership Summit.

Highlighting the vision of the State government to develop Rayalaseema as a global horticulture hub with an investment of ₹1 lakh crore, Mr. Naidu said that fruits grown in the region were being exported to international markets.
The UAE delegation informed Mr. Naidu that it was exploring the possibility of importing shrimp and other aquaculture products from Andhra Pradesh.

Mr. Naidu, during a meeting with Japanese Ambassador Keiichi Ono, discussed industrial investments, skill development, critical minerals, steel industry, green energy and other areas of mutual cooperation.

items.title: State Highways to open FOB to connect railway station and bus terminus in Tiruvannamalai
points: Officials of the State Highways Department, which executed the multi-crore work along with Southern Railway, said that the new bridge will help commuters reach the railway station safely.
At present, commuters from the newly opened bus terminus have to cross the busy Chittoor - Cuddalore High Road to reach the railway station.
“Except for a few trial runs for the escalators, the new steel bridge is almost ready for opening before Maha Deepam day, as it will help thousands of devotees cross the tracks safely,” R.
Sasikumar, Assistant Engineer (AE), State Highways, told The Hindu.
Highways officials said that after approval of the Southern Railway, the State Highways Department laid tiled floors on the new bridge.
Funded under the Chief Minister Road Development Plan 2024-25, the new bridge is 70-metre-long, six-metre-tall, and 20-feet-wide.
In December 2025, former Chief Minister M.K.
Stalin inaugurated the ₹34-crore modern bus terminus.
